title: TERE4AI v2 runtime input: AI system features
description: Structured facts about the consumer's AI system, provided by the human or coding agent. classify_ai_system consumes this; it never guesses missing facts, it reports them in missing_facts (docs/architecture.md Sections 7 and 8). Free-text description is context only; classification decisions rest on the structured fields.

description.description: Plain-language description of the system (context; not the decision basis)

domain.description: Primary domain, free vocabulary (e.g. healthcare, education, employment, law_enforcement, migration, justice, banking, insurance, critical_infrastructure, consumer)

purposes.description: What the system is intended to do, short phrases

autonomy.description: Does the output merely inform a human decision (advisory) or drive it

flags.description: Boolean facts. Absent flag = unknown, which is NOT treated as false for prohibition-relevant flags; unknowns surface in missing_facts.

x-annex-iii-areas.1: Biometrics, in so far as their use is permitted under relevant Union or national law
x-annex-iii-areas.4: Employment, workers’ management and access to self-employment
x-annex-iii-areas.5: Access to and enjoyment of essential private services and essential public services and benefits
x-annex-iii-areas.6: Law enforcement, in so far as their use is permitted under relevant Union or national law
x-annex-iii-areas.7: Migration, asylum and border control management, in so far as their use is permitted under relevant Union or national law
x-annex-iii-areas.8: Administration of justice and democratic processes

biometric_categorisation.description: Article 5(1)(g) practice, the Act's words: 'biometric categorisation systems that categorise individually natural persons based on their biometric data to deduce or infer their race, political opinions, trade union membership, religious or philosophical beliefs, sex life or sexual orientation'. True only for those traits. Categorisation by other sensitive or protected attributes is biometric_categorisation_sensitive_or_protected_attributes; the general system is biometric_categorisation_system. When true, those two are true as well. Absence leaves the ban unsettled.

biometric_categorisation_system.description: Article 3(40), the Act's words: 'biometric categorisation system means an AI system for the purpose of assigning natural persons to specific categories on the basis of their biometric data, unless it is ancillary to another commercial service and strictly necessary for objective technical reasons'. A system that is ancillary to another commercial service and strictly necessary for objective technical reasons is not one (false). Triggers the Article 50(3) information duty. If this is false, biometric_categorisation (Article 5(1)(g)) is false too, since point (g) uses the defined term.

causes_significant_harm.description: Article 5(1)(a)/(b) qualifier, the Act's words: 'in a manner that causes or is reasonably likely to cause that person, another person or group of persons significant harm' (point (a); point (b) reads the same for that person or another person). The subliminal/manipulative or vulnerability-exploiting practice causes or is reasonably likely to cause significant harm. Prohibited only where this holds; false means the point does not prohibit it. Absence leaves the ban unsettled.

social_score_detrimental_treatment.description: Article 5(1)(c) qualifier, the Act's words: 'detrimental or unfavourable treatment of certain natural persons or groups of persons in social contexts that are unrelated to the contexts in which the data was originally generated or collected' or treatment 'that is unjustified or disproportionate to their social behaviour or its gravity'. The social scoring leads to such treatment. False means the point does not prohibit it; absence leaves the ban unsettled.

supports_human_assessment_on_verifiable_.description: Article 5(1)(d) exception, the Act's words: 'this prohibition shall not apply to AI systems used to support the human assessment of the involvement of a person in a criminal activity, which is already based on objective and verifiable facts directly linked to a criminal activity'. True means the prohibition does not apply. Facts that are not directly linked to a criminal activity do not meet the exception.

emotion_recognition_medical_or_safety.description: Article 5(1)(f) exception, the Act's words: 'except where the use of the AI system is intended to be put in place or into the market for medical or safety reasons'. The workplace/education emotion recognition is intended for medical or safety reasons. True means the prohibition does not apply.

biometric_categorisation_lawful_or_law_e.description: Article 5(1)(g) exception, the Act's words: 'this prohibition does not cover any labelling or filtering of lawfully acquired biometric datasets, such as images, based on biometric data or categorizing of biometric data in the area of law enforcement'. True means the prohibition does not apply. A law-enforcement user alone does not meet the exception: the system must label or filter lawfully acquired biometric datasets, or categorise biometric data in the area of law enforcement.

rtrb_strictly_necessary_authorised.description: Article 5(1)(h) carve-out, the Act's words: 'unless and in so far as such use is strictly necessary for one of the following objectives'. The real-time remote biometric identification for law enforcement is strictly necessary for one of the objectives in (i) to (iii) and duly authorised. True means the practice is conditionally permitted, not prohibited; false or absent leaves the ban in place / unsettled.

law_enforcement_purpose.description: Article 5(1)(h) names the purposes of law enforcement; Article 3(46) defines law enforcement, the Act's words: 'law enforcement means activities carried out by law enforcement authorities or on their behalf for the prevention, investigation, detection or prosecution of criminal offences or the execution of criminal penalties, including safeguarding against and preventing threats to public security'. True means the system is used for those purposes; with real_time_remote_biometric_public true it is the point (h) practice, unless rtrb_strictly_necessary_authorised is true. It is not an Annex III fact: the uses Annex III point 6 lists are separate facts. Absence leaves the point (h) ban unsettled while real_time_remote_biometric_public is true.

real_time_remote_biometric_public.description: Article 5(1)(h) practice, the Act's words: 'the use of real-time remote biometric identification systems in publicly accessible spaces for the purposes of law enforcement'. True means the system identifies persons in publicly accessible spaces as Article 3(42) defines it, the Act's words: 'real-time remote biometric identification system means a remote biometric identification system, whereby the capturing of biometric data, the comparison and the identification all occur without a significant delay'. With law_enforcement_purpose true it is the point (h) practice, unless rtrb_strictly_necessary_authorised is true; it also places the system in Annex III point 1. Absence leaves the ban unsettled.

emotion_recognition_workplace_or_educati.description: Article 5(1)(f) practice, the Act's words: 'the use of AI systems to infer emotions of a natural person in the areas of workplace and education institutions, except where the use of the AI system is intended to be put in place or into the market for medical or safety reasons'. The exception is the separate fact emotion_recognition_medical_or_safety: true there means the prohibition does not apply. Absence leaves the ban unsettled unless that exception is known to hold.

social_scoring.description: Article 5(1)(c) practice, the Act's words: 'the evaluation or classification of natural persons or groups of persons over a certain period of time based on their social behaviour or known, inferred or predicted personal or personality characteristics'. The treatment that makes it prohibited is the separate fact social_score_detrimental_treatment. Absence leaves the ban unsettled unless that element is known to be absent.

subliminal_or_manipulative.description: Article 5(1)(a) practice, the Act's words: 'an AI system that deploys subliminal techniques beyond a person’s consciousness or purposefully manipulative or deceptive techniques, with the objective, or the effect of materially distorting the behaviour of a person or a group of persons'. The significant harm element is the separate fact causes_significant_harm. Absence leaves the ban unsettled unless that element is known to be absent.

exploits_vulnerabilities.description: Article 5(1)(b) practice, the Act's words: 'an AI system that exploits any of the vulnerabilities of a natural person or a specific group of persons due to their age, disability or a specific social or economic situation, with the objective, or the effect, of materially distorting the behaviour of that person or a person belonging to that group'. The significant harm element is the separate fact causes_significant_harm. Absence leaves the ban unsettled unless that element is known to be absent.

predictive_policing_profiling.description: Article 5(1)(d) practice, the Act's words: 'an AI system for making risk assessments of natural persons in order to assess or predict the risk of a natural person committing a criminal offence, based solely on the profiling of a natural person or on assessing their personality traits and characteristics'. The point's exception is the separate fact supports_human_assessment_on_verifiable_facts. Absence leaves the ban unsettled.

facial_image_scraping.description: Article 5(1)(e) practice, the Act's words: 'AI systems that create or expand facial recognition databases through the untargeted scraping of facial images from the internet or CCTV footage'. The point has no exception: true is a confident prohibition. Absence leaves the ban unsettled.

biometric_identification.description: Annex III point 1(a), the Act's words: 'remote biometric identification systems. This shall not include AI systems intended to be used for biometric verification the sole purpose of which is to confirm that a specific natural person is the person he or she claims to be'. Point 1 opens with the words 'Biometrics, in so far as their use is permitted under relevant Union or national law', which limit the area and are not a fact. Article 3(41) defines the system, the Act's words: 'remote biometric identification system means an AI system for the purpose of identifying natural persons, without their active involvement, typically at a distance through the comparison of a person’s biometric data with the biometric data contained in a reference database'. True places the system in Annex III point 1, high-risk under Article 6(2); verification of a claimed identity alone is false. Absence is unknown and blocks a confident minimal answer.

biometric_categorisation_sensitive_or_pr.description: Annex III point 1(b), the Act's words: 'AI systems intended to be used for biometric categorisation, according to sensitive or protected attributes or characteristics based on the inference of those attributes or characteristics'. Point 1 opens with the words 'Biometrics, in so far as their use is permitted under relevant Union or national law', which limit the area and are not a fact. High-risk under Article 6(2). Absence is unknown and blocks a confident minimal answer.

emotion_recognition.description: Annex III point 1(c), the Act's words: 'AI systems intended to be used for emotion recognition'. Point 1 opens with the words 'Biometrics, in so far as their use is permitted under relevant Union or national law', which limit the area and are not a fact. Article 3(39) defines the system, the Act's words: 'emotion recognition system means an AI system for the purpose of identifying or inferring emotions or intentions of natural persons on the basis of their biometric data'. True places the system in Annex III point 1, high-risk under Article 6(2), and triggers the Article 50(3) information duty. Use in the workplace or in education is the separate Article 5(1)(f) fact, emotion_recognition_workplace_or_education.

critical_infrastructure_safety.description: Annex III point 2, the Act's words: 'AI systems intended to be used as safety components in the management and operation of critical digital infrastructure, road traffic, or in the supply of water, gas, heating or electricity'. True places the system in Annex III point 2, high-risk under Article 6(2). Absence is unknown and blocks a confident minimal answer.

annex_iii_3a_admission.description: Annex III point 3(a), the Act's words: 'AI systems intended to be used to determine access or admission or to assign natural persons to educational and vocational training institutions at all levels'. True places the system in Annex III point 3, high-risk under Article 6(2); a system inside an exception the quotation states is false. Absence is unknown and blocks a confident minimal answer.

annex_iii_3b_learning_outcomes.description: Annex III point 3(b), the Act's words: 'AI systems intended to be used to evaluate learning outcomes, including when those outcomes are used to steer the learning process of natural persons in educational and vocational training institutions at all levels'. True places the system in Annex III point 3, high-risk under Article 6(2); a system inside an exception the quotation states is false. Absence is unknown and blocks a confident minimal answer.

annex_iii_3c_education_level.description: Annex III point 3(c), the Act's words: 'AI systems intended to be used for the purpose of assessing the appropriate level of education that an individual will receive or will be able to access, in the context of or within educational and vocational training institutions at all levels'. True places the system in Annex III point 3, high-risk under Article 6(2); a system inside an exception the quotation states is false. Absence is unknown and blocks a confident minimal answer.

annex_iii_3d_test_monitoring.description: Annex III point 3(d), the Act's words: 'AI systems intended to be used for monitoring and detecting prohibited behaviour of students during tests in the context of or within educational and vocational training institutions at all levels'. True places the system in Annex III point 3, high-risk under Article 6(2); a system inside an exception the quotation states is false. Absence is unknown and blocks a confident minimal answer.

annex_iii_4a_recruitment.description: Annex III point 4(a), the Act's words: 'AI systems intended to be used for the recruitment or selection of natural persons, in particular to place targeted job advertisements, to analyse and filter job applications, and to evaluate candidates'. True places the system in Annex III point 4, high-risk under Article 6(2); a system inside an exception the quotation states is false. Absence is unknown and blocks a confident minimal answer.

annex_iii_4b_work_relationships.description: Annex III point 4(b), the Act's words: 'AI systems intended to be used to make decisions affecting terms of work-related relationships, the promotion or termination of work-related contractual relationships, to allocate tasks based on individual behaviour or personal traits or characteristics or to monitor and evaluate the performance and behaviour of persons in such relationships'. True places the system in Annex III point 4, high-risk under Article 6(2); a system inside an exception the quotation states is false. Absence is unknown and blocks a confident minimal answer.

annex_iii_5a_public_benefits.description: Annex III point 5(a), the Act's words: 'AI systems intended to be used by public authorities or on behalf of public authorities to evaluate the eligibility of natural persons for essential public assistance benefits and services, including healthcare services, as well as to grant, reduce, revoke, or reclaim such benefits and services'. True places the system in Annex III point 5, high-risk under Article 6(2); a system inside an exception the quotation states is false. Absence is unknown and blocks a confident minimal answer.

creditworthiness_evaluation.description: Annex III point 5(b), the Act's words: 'AI systems intended to be used to evaluate the creditworthiness of natural persons or establish their credit score, with the exception of AI systems used for the purpose of detecting financial fraud'. FRIA-relevant (Article 27(1)).

life_health_insurance_risk_pricing.description: Annex III point 5(c), the Act's words: 'AI systems intended to be used for risk assessment and pricing in relation to natural persons in the case of life and health insurance'. FRIA-relevant (Article 27(1)).

annex_iii_5d_emergency_calls.description: Annex III point 5(d), the Act's words: 'AI systems intended to evaluate and classify emergency calls by natural persons or to be used to dispatch, or to establish priority in the dispatching of, emergency first response services, including by police, firefighters and medical aid, as well as of emergency healthcare patient triage systems'. True places the system in Annex III point 5, high-risk under Article 6(2); a system inside an exception the quotation states is false. Absence is unknown and blocks a confident minimal answer.

annex_iii_6a_victim_risk.description: Annex III point 6(a), the Act's words: 'AI systems intended to be used by or on behalf of law enforcement authorities, or by Union institutions, bodies, offices or agencies in support of law enforcement authorities or on their behalf to assess the risk of a natural person becoming the victim of criminal offences'. Point 6 opens with the words 'Law enforcement, in so far as their use is permitted under relevant Union or national law', which limit the area and are not a fact. True places the system in Annex III point 6, high-risk under Article 6(2); a system inside an exception the quotation states is false. Absence is unknown and blocks a confident minimal answer.

annex_iii_6b_polygraphs.description: Annex III point 6(b), the Act's words: 'AI systems intended to be used by or on behalf of law enforcement authorities or by Union institutions, bodies, offices or agencies in support of law enforcement authorities as polygraphs or similar tools'. Point 6 opens with the words 'Law enforcement, in so far as their use is permitted under relevant Union or national law', which limit the area and are not a fact. True places the system in Annex III point 6, high-risk under Article 6(2); a system inside an exception the quotation states is false. Absence is unknown and blocks a confident minimal answer.

annex_iii_6c_evidence_reliability.description: Annex III point 6(c), the Act's words: 'AI systems intended to be used by or on behalf of law enforcement authorities, or by Union institutions, bodies, offices or agencies, in support of law enforcement authorities to evaluate the reliability of evidence in the course of the investigation or prosecution of criminal offences'. Point 6 opens with the words 'Law enforcement, in so far as their use is permitted under relevant Union or national law', which limit the area and are not a fact. True places the system in Annex III point 6, high-risk under Article 6(2); a system inside an exception the quotation states is false. Absence is unknown and blocks a confident minimal answer.

annex_iii_6d_offending_risk.description: Annex III point 6(d), the Act's words: 'AI systems intended to be used by law enforcement authorities or on their behalf or by Union institutions, bodies, offices or agencies in support of law enforcement authorities for assessing the risk of a natural person offending or re-offending not solely on the basis of the profiling of natural persons as referred to in Article 3(4) of Directive (EU) 2016/680, or to assess personality traits and characteristics or past criminal behaviour of natural persons or groups'. Point 6 opens with the words 'Law enforcement, in so far as their use is permitted under relevant Union or national law', which limit the area and are not a fact. True places the system in Annex III point 6, high-risk under Article 6(2); a system inside an exception the quotation states is false. Absence is unknown and blocks a confident minimal answer.

annex_iii_6e_profiling.description: Annex III point 6(e), the Act's words: 'AI systems intended to be used by or on behalf of law enforcement authorities or by Union institutions, bodies, offices or agencies in support of law enforcement authorities for the profiling of natural persons as referred to in Article 3(4) of Directive (EU) 2016/680 in the course of the detection, investigation or prosecution of criminal offences'. Point 6 opens with the words 'Law enforcement, in so far as their use is permitted under relevant Union or national law', which limit the area and are not a fact. True places the system in Annex III point 6, high-risk under Article 6(2); a system inside an exception the quotation states is false. Absence is unknown and blocks a confident minimal answer.

annex_iii_7a_polygraphs.description: Annex III point 7(a), the Act's words: 'AI systems intended to be used by or on behalf of competent public authorities or by Union institutions, bodies, offices or agencies as polygraphs or similar tools'. Point 7 opens with the words 'Migration, asylum and border control management, in so far as their use is permitted under relevant Union or national law', which limit the area and are not a fact. True places the system in Annex III point 7, high-risk under Article 6(2); a system inside an exception the quotation states is false. Absence is unknown and blocks a confident minimal answer.

annex_iii_7b_entry_risk.description: Annex III point 7(b), the Act's words: 'AI systems intended to be used by or on behalf of competent public authorities or by Union institutions, bodies, offices or agencies to assess a risk, including a security risk, a risk of irregular migration, or a health risk, posed by a natural person who intends to enter or who has entered into the territory of a Member State'. Point 7 opens with the words 'Migration, asylum and border control management, in so far as their use is permitted under relevant Union or national law', which limit the area and are not a fact. True places the system in Annex III point 7, high-risk under Article 6(2); a system inside an exception the quotation states is false. Absence is unknown and blocks a confident minimal answer.

annex_iii_7c_applications.description: Annex III point 7(c), the Act's words: 'AI systems intended to be used by or on behalf of competent public authorities or by Union institutions, bodies, offices or agencies to assist competent public authorities for the examination of applications for asylum, visa or residence permits and for associated complaints with regard to the eligibility of the natural persons applying for a status, including related assessments of the reliability of evidence'. Point 7 opens with the words 'Migration, asylum and border control management, in so far as their use is permitted under relevant Union or national law', which limit the area and are not a fact. True places the system in Annex III point 7, high-risk under Article 6(2); a system inside an exception the quotation states is false. Absence is unknown and blocks a confident minimal answer.

annex_iii_7d_identification.description: Annex III point 7(d), the Act's words: 'AI systems intended to be used by or on behalf of competent public authorities, or by Union institutions, bodies, offices or agencies, in the context of migration, asylum or border control management, for the purpose of detecting, recognising or identifying natural persons, with the exception of the verification of travel documents'. Point 7 opens with the words 'Migration, asylum and border control management, in so far as their use is permitted under relevant Union or national law', which limit the area and are not a fact. True places the system in Annex III point 7, high-risk under Article 6(2); a system inside an exception the quotation states is false. Absence is unknown and blocks a confident minimal answer.

annex_iii_8a_judicial.description: Annex III point 8(a), the Act's words: 'AI systems intended to be used by a judicial authority or on their behalf to assist a judicial authority in researching and interpreting facts and the law and in applying the law to a concrete set of facts, or to be used in a similar way in alternative dispute resolution'. True places the system in Annex III point 8, high-risk under Article 6(2); a system inside an exception the quotation states is false. Absence is unknown and blocks a confident minimal answer.

annex_iii_8b_elections.description: Annex III point 8(b), the Act's words: 'AI systems intended to be used for influencing the outcome of an election or referendum or the voting behaviour of natural persons in the exercise of their vote in elections or referenda. This does not include AI systems to the output of which natural persons are not directly exposed, such as tools used to organise, optimise or structure political campaigns from an administrative or logistical point of view'. True places the system in Annex III point 8, high-risk under Article 6(2); a system inside an exception the quotation states is false. Absence is unknown and blocks a confident minimal answer.

medical_or_safety_component.description: Article 3(14) as replaced by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 defines a safety component, the Act's words: 'safety component means a component of a product or of an AI system which fulfils a safety function for that product or AI system, or the failure or malfunctioning of which endangers the health and safety of persons or property; for the purposes of this definition, a component fulfils a safety function where its intended purpose is to prevent or mitigate risks to health and safety of persons or property'. Article 6(1a), the Act's words: 'For the purposes of this Regulation, including paragraph 1 of this Article, AI systems that are solely used for non-safety related aspects of user assistance, performance optimisation, service efficiency, automation or convenience or quality control shall not qualify as safety components.' Article 6(1b), the Act's words: 'Notwithstanding paragraph 1a, AI systems the failure or malfunctioning of which would endanger health and safety shall qualify as safety components.' True means the system is such a component, or is itself a product with a safety function (a medical device, for example). It does not decide the level on its own: the Article 6(1) route needs annex_i_covered_product and third_party_conformity_assessment_required, and while those are unknown the answer is undetermined.

interacts_with_natural_persons.description: Article 50(1), the Act's words: 'AI systems intended to interact directly with natural persons'. True triggers the Article 50(1) duty to inform the persons that they are interacting with an AI system, unless this is obvious; the paragraph names its own exceptions.

generates_synthetic_content.description: Article 50(2), the Act's words: 'Providers of AI systems, including general-purpose AI systems, generating synthetic audio, image, video or text content'. True triggers the Article 50(2) duty to mark the outputs as artificially generated or manipulated; the paragraph names its own exceptions.

profiling_of_natural_persons.description: Article 6(3) third subparagraph, the Act's words: 'an AI system referred to in Annex III shall always be considered to be high-risk where the AI system performs profiling of natural persons'. Article 3(52) defines the term, the Act's words: 'profiling means profiling as defined in Article 4, point (4), of Regulation (EU) 2016/679'. True keeps an Annex III system high-risk even when an Article 6(3) condition holds; while it is unknown and a condition holds, the classifier names it as missing.

preparatory_or_narrow_procedural_task.description: Article 6(3) points (a) and (d), the Act's words: 'the AI system is intended to perform a narrow procedural task' and 'the AI system is intended to perform a preparatory task to an assessment relevant for the purposes of the use cases listed in Annex III'. True, with autonomy advisory, marks an Annex III system as an Article 6(3) exception candidate; the derogation is never applied by the classifier, the system stays high-risk.

improves_previous_human_activity.description: Article 6(3) point (b), the Act's words: 'the AI system is intended to improve the result of a previously completed human activity'. True marks an Annex III system as an Article 6(3) exception candidate; the derogation is never applied by the classifier, the system stays high-risk.

detects_patterns_without_replacing_human.description: Article 6(3) point (c), the Act's words: 'the AI system is intended to detect decision-making patterns or deviations from prior decision-making patterns and is not meant to replace or influence the previously completed human assessment, without proper human review'. True marks an Annex III system as an Article 6(3) exception candidate; the derogation is never applied by the classifier, the system stays high-risk.

annex_i_covered_product.description: Article 6(1)(a), the Act's words: 'the AI system is intended to be used as a safety component of a product, or the AI system is itself a product, covered by the Union harmonisation legislation listed in Annex I'. Which AI systems qualify as safety components is narrowed by Article 6(1a), the Act's words: 'AI systems that are solely used for non-safety related aspects of user assistance, performance optimisation, service efficiency, automation or convenience or quality control shall not qualify as safety components', and by Article 6(1b), the Act's words: 'Notwithstanding paragraph 1a, AI systems the failure or malfunctioning of which would endanger health and safety shall qualify as safety components.' True with third_party_conformity_assessment_required true makes the system high-risk under Article 6(1); false rules that route out. Absence leaves the route open, and the answer undetermined unless another rule decides it. Annex I has two sections; annex_i_section_b_legislation names which one lists the product's legislation.

third_party_conformity_assessment_requir.description: Article 6(1)(b), the Act's words: 'the product whose safety component pursuant to point (a) is the AI system, or the AI system itself as a product, is required to undergo a third-party conformity assessment'. Article 6(1c), the Act's words: 'A product that is required to undergo a third-party conformity assessment solely due to risks other than risks to health and safety, in particular risks relating to the distribution of radio spectrum or electromagnetic interference that do not affect health and safety, shall not be considered as fulfilling the condition in paragraph 1, point (b).' Asked only once annex_i_covered_product is true; both true make the system high-risk under Article 6(1), and false rules the route out.

annex_i_section_b_legislation.description: Article 2(2), the Act's words: 'For AI systems classified as high-risk AI systems in accordance with Article 6(1) related to products covered by the Union harmonisation legislation listed in Section B of Annex I, only Article 6(1), Article 60a and Articles 102 to 112 shall apply.' True means the Union harmonisation legislation covering the product is listed in Section B of Annex I (points 13 to 21, among them motor vehicles, civil aviation and, since Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, machinery); false means it is listed in Section A (points 2 to 12). Asked only once annex_i_covered_product is true. It does not change the level: a system high-risk under Article 6(1) is high_risk under either section, and the section decides the requirements served (Section B: the provisions Article 2(2) names, not the Chapter III requirements). Absence leaves the section unknown, which is never read as Section B.

generates_nonconsensual_intimate_materia.description: Article 5(1)(ba), inserted by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 and applying from 2 December 2026 (Article 113, third paragraph, point (a)), the Act's words: 'the placing on the market, the putting into service or the use of an AI system that generates or manipulates realistic images, videos, audio or similar material of an identifiable natural person’s intimate parts, or of an identifiable natural person engaged in sexually explicit activities, without that person’s freely-given, specific, informed, unambiguous and explicit consent for that generation or manipulation'. Article 5(1a) limits the prohibition to a system whose intended purpose is that generation or manipulation, or for which it is a reasonably foreseeable and reproducible outcome without adequate safeguards, and to a deployer who uses the system for that purpose; Article 5(1b), the Act's words: 'an AI system that manipulates material in a way that does not increase the exposure of any depicted intimate parts or alter the nature of any depicted sexually explicit activities shall not constitute manipulation'. Set true only when the complete practice holds; absence leaves the ban unsettled.

generates_csam.description: Article 5(1)(bb), inserted by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 and applying from 2 December 2026 (Article 113, third paragraph, point (a)), the Act's words: 'the placing on the market, the putting into service or the use of an AI system that generates or manipulates material or performance within the meaning of Article 2, points (c) and (e), of Directive 2011/93/EU, except where a ‘without right’ defence applies under national law'. Article 5(1a) limits the prohibition in the same way as for point (ba). Set true only when the complete practice holds; absence leaves the ban unsettled.

deployer_kind.description: Who operates it (e.g. public_authority, private_company, individual). Free vocabulary, context only; the FRIA rule never reads it because it cannot be mapped deterministically onto the Article 27(1) legal categories. Use the structured deployer object for those.

deployer.description: Structured facts about the deploying organisation, phrased in the Article 27(1) categories. Absent fact = unknown, never treated as false; unknowns surface in the fria block, not guessed.

body_governed_by_public_law.description: The deployer is a body governed by public law (Article 27(1)).

private_entity_providing_public_services.description: The deployer is a private entity providing public services (Article 27(1)).
